name: Marchetti-Oyelaran
hardPart: A 68-year-old retiree and a 41-year-old spouse; a new power of attorney arrived from the spouse's sibling; children from the first marriage are the named beneficiaries

goals.assumption: 24 months of spending at $19K a month
Stated intent: equal treatment of L. and F., not yet documented

contactHistory.summary: G. asked about updating beneficiaries; said F. would follow up
Annual review; both attended; no changes

notes.text: F. Oyelaran's brother delivered a signed power of attorney for G. and asked for online access to the accounts.
G. sounded uncertain about which children he meant. Follow up with both spouses on the line.

tasks.text: Confirm the power of attorney with G. directly, by phone on the number on file
Ask Legal whether the POA is on the firm's form

supervisory.note: A power of attorney presented in person by a relative of the younger spouse, with a request for account access, on an account whose oldest holder is 68.

messages.text: This is not what we were told at the review. My brother is only trying to help G. with the paperwork and now you want another call. I'm unhappy with how this is being handled.
I understand, and I'm sorry it feels that way. Any change to who may act on G.'s account needs G. on the phone with us first. That protects him and it protects you. I'll call tomorrow at ten.
